claim: A source-specific V53 comparison finds external molecular and structural plausibility context for the coupled HLA-II/CD74/MIF axis, but no same-definition external validation or contradiction of the project-grounded MIF/CD74 therapeutic null.
decision_relevant_result: External structure and mechanism records make physical plausibility concrete but do not supply the missing human component-specific association or stable favorable intervention direction. The grounded target non-promotion is unchanged.

grounded_reference.status: Project data support a recurrent tone-loaded APC receptor-state context but not MIF-specific causality, receptor-specific adjusted response, stable therapy direction, or target promotion.

project_use: Segregated convergence/contradiction context only; the project-grounded audit remains the evidence.
relationship_note: Convergence raises plausibility context and tension flags follow-up; neither changes the grounded finding.

relationships.interpretation: The source places MIF, CD74, and CXCR4 in an MS B-cell context but does not reproduce the multi-modality axis or test treatment direction.

relationships.grounded_component: CD74 bridge between HLA-II and receptor-state modules
relationships.interpretation: The annotation supports molecular bridge plausibility but is not MS-specific and does not test the project axis.
The 8VRW experimental complex supplies physical CD74-HLA-DR15 interface context, not evidence for MIF causality or an MS intervention direction.

relationships.grounded_component: no MIF-specific causal or therapeutic claim in held human data
relationships.interpretation: The animal-model intervention creates mechanistic tension worth noting, but species, construct, endpoint, and evidence type differ; it is not a same-definition contradiction.
Experimental inhibitor-bound MIF structures establish physical inhibitor compatibility only. They do not establish favorable MS direction or component-specific project support.

relationships.grounded_component: MIF-CD74 receptor interaction as a therapeutic mechanism
